judged_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy-string derived from two independent env vars, not a declared boolean, and gate logic is duplicated across three files with slightly different conditions (webhook handler gates only on the flag, refreshOAuthTokens also requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and userId, parseRefreshTokenResponse requires the endpoint). A self-hoster who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET + encryption key but no sync endpoint gets the ingest webhook active while refresh paths still use provider refresh — a half-enabled mixed state that is hard to reason about; the next app wired to this feature must remember to replicate the three-part condition correctly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts), which yields a string/undefined rather than an explicit boolean. The gating conditions are indeed inconsistent/duplicated: the webhook handler enables the endpoint solely based on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts), while `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally requires `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and `userId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` also changes behavior only when the endpoint is set (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). This creates a diff-grounded maintainability/feature-flag consistency concern (mixed configurations are possible) rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.
